channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Defense Ministry Investigation Uncovers 37 Criminal Cases
item.description: An extensive inspection by Kazakhstan's Ministry of Defense has revealed 37 criminal cases. The commission examined 104 ministry facilities, with ongoing audits into the effective use of budget funds. Investigations into violations of military personnel safety, service conditions, and property preservation are underway.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Prosecutor General Clarifies Laws on Online Extremism
item.description: The Prosecutor General's Office of Kyrgyzstan has issued clarifications on responsibility for storing and distributing extremist materials online. Actions like storing or publishing prohibited content on social media can lead to administrative fines or criminal charges under Kyrgyz law.

item.title: Kazakhstan President and King of Jordan Hold Talks
item.description: The President of Kazakhstan and the King of Jordan held negotiations in Astana. The Kazakh leader described the official visit of Abdullah II as a testament to strong bonds of friendship, mutual respect, and solidarity between the countries. Both sides expressed high regard for the established political dialogue.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Prioritize National Interests in OPEC+ Deal Compliance
item.description: Kazakhstan will continue to be guided by its national interests while adhering to the OPEC+ deal, especially at current oil prices, stated the Minister of Energy. He noted that the world needs additional oil volumes. Kazakhstan plans to produce around 99 million tons of oil in 2027.

item.title: Kazakh President Calls Jordan a Reliable Partner in the Arab World
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev described Jordan as a time-tested and reliable partner for Kazakhstan in the Arab world during talks with King Abdullah II. He highlighted the strengthened political dialogue and potential for expanded cooperation in economic, cultural, and humanitarian spheres.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Welcomes King of Jordan to Astana
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev welcomed King Abdullah II of Jordan to Kazakhstan upon his arrival at Astana airport for an official visit. A guard of honor was present during the welcoming ceremony. The visit follows an invitation from the Kazakh head of state.

item.title: Kazpost and Kazakhtelecom ordered to pay monthly compensation to woman injured by falling roof
item.description: In the Zhambyl region, a court has ordered Kazpost and Kazakhtelecom to pay a woman 177,000 tenge monthly after a roof collapsed on her. The companies must compensate her for lost earnings until retirement age. The incident occurred in May 2023 when strong winds tore off the roof of a building owned by both companies.

item.title: Zhanna Nemtsova Sentenced to Four Years in Absentia in Russia
item.description: A Moscow court has sentenced Zhanna Nemtsova, daughter of politician Boris Nemtsov, to four years in prison in absentia. She was charged with organizing the activities of an "undesirable" organization, the Boris Nemtsov Foundation for Freedom, which was designated as such in April 2024.

item.title: Kazakhstan formally requests Russia to reopen Druzhba oil pipeline to Germany
item.description: Kazakhstan has officially asked Russia to resume oil shipments to Germany via the Druzhba pipeline, which has been halted for six months. Energy Minister Yerlan Akkenzhenov personally delivered the request to Russian officials. Kazakhstan possesses the technical capacity for deliveries and awaits Moscow's response.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank notes slowing inflation for most goods and services
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank reports a slowdown in price growth for most goods and services within the consumer basket. Deputy Chairman Nodirbek Achilov stated that the trend of prices not falling after rising is not currently observed, citing the currency exchange rate as an example.

item.title: Kazakhstan Victims Compensation Fund Pays Out Only 9% of Revenue
item.description: Kazakhstan's Victims Compensation Fund has collected over 9.3 billion tenge ($20.6 million) in eight years but disbursed only 9% to crime victims. A parliament member proposed increasing payments or expanding eligibility, citing figures that show 5,500 victims received just over 855 million tenge ($1.9 million) by July 2026, with 8.5 billion tenge ($18.8 million) remaining in the fund.

item.title: US Open to Mediating Taliban-Pakistan Conflict, Welcomes Pakistan's Anti-Terror Stance
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio indicated Washington's willingness to mediate the conflict between the Taliban and Pakistan if an opportunity arises, while also welcoming Pakistan's efforts against terrorism. Both Pakistan and the Taliban have expressed openness to US mediation, with the Taliban showing greater enthusiasm. Several regional and international powers are also involved in mediation efforts.

item.title: Uzbekistan Achieves Record Cotton Harvest of Over Five Million Tons
item.description: Uzbekistan has harvested over five million tons of raw cotton in 2026, a record since its independence in 1991. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attributed this success to increased yields and mechanization, despite reduced planting areas. Farmers are expected to profit significantly.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reforms Labor Migration System to Focus on Skilled Workers
item.description: Uzbekistan is overhauling its labor migration system to prioritize skilled and language-proficient workers for specific foreign job demands. The initiative includes local registration, grants for training institutions, and partnerships with foreign recruitment agencies. Private agencies will now handle overseas employment.

item.title: French Assembly Speaker Calls Taliban Policies 'Gender Apartheid,' Urges Action
item.description: French National Assembly Speaker Yaël Braun-Pivet described the Taliban's treatment of women and girls as "gender apartheid" after meeting with Afghan activists. She called for urgent action, stating that women and girls have been systematically removed from public life and deprived of their rights. Braun-Pivet urged practical measures to confront the "bitter reality" of their situation.

item.title: Kazakh Officials Must Prove Elimination of Corruption Risks Under New Regulations
item.description: Kazakh officials will face stricter requirements to prove the elimination of corruption risks, according to a new draft order from the Agency for Civil Service Affairs. The changes aim to clarify the assessment of implemented recommendations, requiring concrete results and supporting documents before risks can be removed from monitoring.

item.title: Jordan's King Abdullah II Arrives in Kazakhstan for Official Visit
item.description: King Abdullah II of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan has arrived in Kazakhstan for an official visit. A welcoming ceremony was held at Akorda, attended by Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. Military helicopters flew over Akorda, displaying the state flags of Kazakhstan and Jordan. The King was met at the airport by the President.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Sunflower Husk Used for European Power Plants
item.description: Kazakhstan is increasing its export of sunflower husk, previously considered a production waste, for use as biofuel in European power plants. Export revenue from granulated sunflower husk rose 6.15 times to $3.4 million in the first nine months of 2026. Poland is the largest buyer, accounting for about 98% of exports in 2025.

item.title: Over 300,000 in Kyrgyzstan Used Self-Exclusion on Loans in One Year
item.description: Over 300,000 people in Kyrgyzstan have utilized the voluntary self-exclusion mechanism for obtaining loans within the past year. As of November 1, 2026, 200,100 individuals still maintain an active restriction. This service, available via the "Tunduk" mobile app, allows citizens to prevent financial institutions from issuing them new loans.

item.title: Tenge Weakens Against Dollar in Kazakhstan Trading Session
item.description: The US dollar depreciated by 0.85 tenge during the day's trading on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange (KASE), reaching an average rate of 451.87 tenge. The official rate set by the National Bank is 452.91 tenge. Exchange offices in Astana bought dollars at 448 tenge and sold them at 455 tenge.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Double Uranium Production by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to double its uranium production by 2030. During a meeting chaired by the President, plans were also reviewed to increase the production of strategic metals to over $2.7 billion and attract $1.1 billion in investments for tungsten deep processing projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ready to Export Up to 500,000 Tons of Wheat to Israel
item.description: Kazakhstan is prepared to consider supplying between 200,000 and 500,000 tons of food wheat and other agricultural products to Israel. This was discussed at the tenth meeting of the Kazakhstan-Israel Intergovernmental Commission in Jerusalem. "Prodcorporation" is ready to discuss long-term contracts based on Israeli market demand.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Defense's Fifth Attempt to Remove Judge in Bokayev Case Denied
item.description: In Kazakhstan, defense lawyers for civil activist Sanzhar Bokayev were denied their fifth request to remove Judge Zhanat Abenova, citing suspicions of bias. The prosecution alleges Bokayev defrauded 42 million tenge in 2018 through a scheme involving a gas vehicle mileage event. The defense argues the court is not adhering to the scope of the investigation.

item.title: Europe Experiences New Wave of Bomb Threats on Passenger Planes
item.description: Several European airlines received bomb threat messages on November 5, leading to diverted flights and security checks. A flight from Dublin to Rome was diverted to a military airbase in Normandy. Finnair confirmed threats to two flights from Helsinki, which landed safely. Wizz Air and LOT also reported threats on flights to Vienna and Brussels respectively.

item.title: Kazakh Businessmen Secure $100 Million in Agreements at China International Import Expo
item.description: Kazakhstani businessmen have secured agreements worth $100 million at the China International Import Expo (CIIE). The expo provides a platform for international trade and investment, fostering economic cooperation between Kazakhstan and China. This achievement highlights the growing trade relations between the two countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Increase Uranium Production to 15,000 Tons Annually by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to increase its annual uranium production to 15,000 tons by 2030, as part of a strategy to boost production of 16 critical metals. The country aims to increase production of critical minerals, which have seen a 10% annual market growth, compared to traditional metals' 1%. This initiative is part of a broader plan to utilize mineral resources effectively.

item.title: Over Half of Afghan Primary School-Age Children Are Not Enrolled in School, UN Reports
item.description: A new report by UNESCO and UNICEF indicates that more than half of Afghanistan's primary school-age children are not in formal education. The report highlights challenges including population growth, recurring emergencies, insufficient investment, and the return of Afghan migrants. Over 2.6 million girls are unable to continue studies beyond sixth grade.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allocates Funds for University Student Education in 2026-2027 Academic Year
item.description: Kazakhstan will allocate between 803,900 and 1.2 million tenge per student for state-funded higher education in the 2026-2027 academic year. The exact amount varies by specialty and university status, with medical fields receiving more funding than social sciences. A total of 89,457 state grants are planned.

item.title: Death Toll Rises to 42 After Russian Airstrike in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia Region
item.description: The death toll from a Russian airstrike on the village of Kamyshevakha in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region on November 2 has increased to 42. Search and rescue operations are ongoing. Authorities have identified 12 victims, with 59 people initially reported missing. The strike damaged an educational facility and other buildings.

item.title: Uzbekistan and USA Develop Investment Cooperation in Geology
item.description: Uzbekistan and the USA are enhancing investment cooperation in the geology sector. Discussions focused on efficient use of critical minerals, prospects for investment, and expanding geological research. Both sides emphasized strengthening mutually beneficial cooperation and implementing promising projects.

item.title: Wall Street Journal: Houthis Demand $51 Billion to End War with Saudi Arabia
item.description: The Wall Street Journal reports that Houthi rebels have demanded $51 billion from Saudi Arabia as a condition to end the ongoing conflict. The report details the significant financial sum sought by the Houthi movement in exchange for peace.

item.title: Jordan's King and Tajikistan's President to Visit Astana
item.description: King Abdullah II bin Al-Hussein of Jordan and President Emomali Rahmon of Tajikistan are scheduled to visit Astana in early November. The visits will include participation in the Aqaba Process summit, focusing on regional cooperation and security.

item.title: Tigers Reintroduced to Kazakhstan Nature Reserve
item.description: Kazakhstan has reintroduced two tigers into a nature reserve, marking the return of these large predators after an 80-year absence. The male tigers, named Amur, were released into the 'Ile-Balkhash' state reserve. A female tiger, Umit, was previously released and has adapted well.

item.title: Kazakhstan Agrees to Increase Air Flights with China and Uzbekistan
item.description: Kazakhstan has reached an agreement with China and Uzbekistan to increase the number of air flights between the countries. This development is expected to enhance connectivity and facilitate travel and trade between the nations. Further details on the specific routes and frequency increases were not immediately available.

item.title: Kazakhstan Strengthens Tax Control Over Mobile Transfers
item.description: Kazakhstan has intensified tax control over mobile transfers, sending over 25,000 notifications to citizens. Individuals receiving 100 or more mobile transfers totaling over 360 MCI (approximately 1,557,000 tenge in 2026) within three months are now subject to tax scrutiny. This measure aims to ensure compliance with business registration requirements.

item.title: UN Women Chief: Gender Equality Must Be Central to UN Development Efforts
item.description: Sima Bahous, Executive Director of UN Women, stated that gender equality must be a core priority for the United Nations' development work. Speaking at the UN Global Meeting of Resident Coordinators, she emphasized its fundamental importance. Bahous thanked coordinators for their efforts, noting ongoing challenges for women and girls in Afghanistan.

item.title: Tajikistan Begins Reconstruction of 54.1 km Baljuvon-Sari Khosor Road
item.description: Tajikistan has commenced the first phase of the Baljuvon-Sari Khosor road reconstruction project, covering an initial 12 kilometers. The Ministry of Transport reported that 39 units of specialized equipment and 115 workers, including 40 Chinese citizens, are involved. The project, financed by the EBRD, aims to improve regional transport infrastructure and socio-economic conditions.

item.title: 28-Year-Old Man Fatally Shot in Sheberghan, Jawzjan Province
item.description: A 28-year-old man was shot dead in Sheberghan, the capital of Jawzjan province, according to local sources. The Taliban stated the incident occurred at a bakery following a family dispute, and four individuals have been arrested. This killing contributes to rising concerns over insecurity and mysterious violence across Afghanistan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Protests Forced Recruitment of Citizen into Russian Military
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's embassy in Russia has sent a note to the Russian Foreign Ministry requesting the swift return of a Kyrgyz citizen, Elistan Toktogulov, allegedly coerced into military service through fraudulent means. Kyrgyzstan's MFA is investigating the circumstances and seeking accountability for those responsible, urging citizens to carefully review contracts.

item.title: Tajikistan Seeks to Expand Industrial Cooperation with South Korea
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Industry and New Technologies met with the South Korean Ambassador to discuss expanding industrial and investment cooperation. Key focus areas included attracting South Korean investment and implementing modern technologies in Tajikistan's industrial sector. Both sides emphasized the need for a joint action plan and prioritized investment projects.
